The subshell call at :1045 sits in a non-tested position under set -e, and with_state_lock has bare callers today: rmw_state:654 is rmw_state's last command, and rmw_state is called bare from roughly thirty mutators. On those paths a non-zero locked body aborts the shell AT :1045, so _EDM_TRAP_DEPTH is never reset to 0, the saved EXIT/INT/TERM/HUP traps are never restored, and the return never runs -- worse than write_atomic's version was, because what gets skipped is lock-release bookkeeping rather than a temp-file removal. The flock branch four lines above does it correctly at :944 with the rationale spelled out at :940-942, and write_atomic:581-586, rewritten by CA-134's remediation this round, states the rule in general terms. Fix: declare ec before the call and guard the capture on the same statement, then add a case that hides flock from PATH, calls rmw_state bare with a failing filter, and asserts both a non-zero exit and that the lockdir is gone.

get_session_tokens_since reports its new torn-line counter THROUGH attribution_mode (:341 and :371), a field that is a two-value enum everywhere else: plugins/edm/CLAUDE.md:427 and :436, the CLAUDE.md state-field table's audit-round row, and a wave6-smoke.sh:3427-3434 case that fails on anything else. Introduced by the CA-060 remediation. Three consequences: one torn line in a live-appended session JSONL -- the exact condition CA-060 was filed about, and routine when phase-complete runs while Claude Code is still appending -- fails the blocking test:smoke job; the out-of-enum value is written into committed state at :1918 and :3391 and rendered by metrics-report, with no state_anomalies class covering it; and it destroys the information the field exists to carry, because a reader can no longer tell whether an unparseable figure came from the scoped driving-session read or the whole-directory fallback, which is the only question attribution_mode was added to answer. Fix: keep the enum two-valued, report the parse failure in a new unparseable_lines field threaded through both consumers, and add a TORN_TOKEN_LINES informational anomaly.

ESCALATED to P1 on three-lens corroboration: the CA-023 fix normalizes srd_root for a leading dot-slash only, so a trailing slash or an absolute value silently disables ALL commit-time artifact enforcement -- a security control that fails OPEN with no diagnostic. With EDM_SRD_ROOT set to a trailing-slash value the awk test compares the staged path's first five characters against a doubled separator, which never matches any real path; with an absolute value nothing matches because git diff --cached --name-only prints repository-relative paths. Either way the derived prefix set is empty, the early-exit guard fires, and every commit passes unlinted. The asymmetry is what makes this a defect rather than user error: edm-state tolerates the same values because it joins paths that the filesystem collapses, and a direct edm-lint-artifacts invocation works fine, so an operator sees every manual path work while automatic enforcement silently disappears. Third defect in the same line: awk -v applies escape-sequence processing to the assignment, so a backslash in the path is mangled before the comparison -- the POSIX-awk hazard _harness.sh:285-290 already documents and works around via ENVIRON. Fix: strip trailing slashes, refuse an absolute value loudly, pass the root through the environment rather than -v, and add a positive-control case (the existing wave7-smoke.sh:3370 assertion pins the literal matcher and cannot catch this).

this round's own remediation INVERTED two statements inside the EDM-HELP sentinel block -- that is, inside --help, the one operator-facing surface -- and they now tell an operator that working enforcement is broken. :43-44 still says the PreToolUse git-commit hook blocks on any non-zero exit and prints one generic remediation line for both failure classes, which CA-011's fix replaced with distinct exit-1 and exit-2 handling and two different messages. :53-55 still says the hook's staged-path matcher is the literal SRD prefix so relocating srd_root drops hook enforcement unless the hook is updated too, which CA-023's fix replaced with a derived root -- and plugins/edm/CLAUDE.md:656-659 was updated to state the opposite, so the two documents now contradict each other and the one a contributor reads first is the wrong one. Note also the internal contradiction: :42 says direct callers, CI and tests can distinguish exit 1 from exit 2, and the very next sentence denies it. This is CA-017's own class reopened by the remediation rather than closed by it. Fix: rewrite both passages to the current contract, and make the same edit to CLAUDE.md's bin/ table row for edm-lint-artifacts.

the new EDM_EVAL_KEEP_RUNS retention loop recursively removes directories it does not own and mis-computes its own keep window. (1) No ownership filter: run directories are named with a timestamp-and-SHA pattern that the prune applies NOWHERE, while --out is a documented first-class flag whose help text says only where the run is written -- so pointing it at a directory holding twelve unrelated subdirectories silently deletes the oldest two, recursively, on the success path. (2) Off-by-N between the guard and the list: run_total counts with find restricted to directories while the stale list positions by ls -1t, which lists all non-hidden entries, so any regular file in the root consumes one of the protected slots and slides the offset window down into directories still inside the keep set; the directory test at :564 prevents deleting non-directories but does nothing to correct the offset, making the miscount silent rather than preventing it. Today's default root holds only a hidden file so the default path is safe, but BOTH documented workflows use --out (evals/baseline/README.md:37 for three consecutive baseline captures, evals/README.md:38-41). Fix: derive the count and the window from one run-id-filtered directory listing, and require an explicit opt-in before pruning a user-supplied --out root; document the retention behaviour on the --out help line.

the CA-035 remediation introduced the only bc invocation anywhere in plugins/edm/, and no pinned CI image installs it: all eleven apk add lines in .gitlab-ci.yml (:85, :133, :152, :165, :191, :222, :268, :325, :360, :389, :438) install only bash, jq, git and shellcheck, and bc is a separate Alpine package absent from the declared set for both test:smoke and test:smoke-bash32. the CA-164 fix replaced the inline lens JSONL schema with a POINTER to each lens's own JSONL Line Format section, and this round the pointer had nothing to resolve against: the delivered prompts named one output path (the markdown), carried no JSONL bullet and no schema pointer, and the delivered agent definitions contained no such section (CA-130's stale-cache artifact). current_step has three consumers and NO producer anywhere in the prompt surface. _p95's docstring says integer p95 (nearest-rank) but the body truncates with awk's int() where nearest-rank requires a ceiling, so NO mode reports a p95: --subcommands returns the 9th of 10 samples (the p90), --phase-complete, --ledger, --session-start and --lint return the 4th of 5 (the p80), and --mermaid-ratio returns the 2nd of 3 (the median). The slowest sample is always discarded, so every figure is biased LOW against the budget it is compared to. These outputs are the committed evidence for the 3,000 ms commit-path and 60,000 ms CI budgets in plugins/edm/CLAUDE.md, the millisecond figures in EDMV3-T67's ACs, and the mermaid ratio quoted in CHANGELOG.md, under a harness header at :7 asserting that every mode is a real measurement and no numbers are invented. Fix: add one line so the index rounds up when the product is fractional, then separately raise the sample counts -- three and five samples cannot support a 95th percentile at all, so either take twenty or rename the emitted key to a maximum and update the four consuming documents -- and re-run every mode to re-record the published figures.

--mermaid-ratio's divide-by-zero guard substitutes a WRONG answer for a missing one: when the baseline p95 is 0 the printed ratio is the numerator itself, a duration in milliseconds, labelled as a multiplier and compared against the 1.40x budget. A zero baseline is not exotic -- _now's documented perl-less fallback at :34-41 has whole-second resolution, so on any Alpine-like image without perl a lint pass over the 30-file fixture measures 0 ms for every sample and _p95 returns 0 -- so the mode prints something like a 40x ratio, an apparent 28-fold budget breach that is purely a timer artifact, in the one mode whose entire output is a single ratio, on exactly the image class CA-158's fallback was added to support. Fix: when either p95 is zero or negative, print an UNMEASURABLE diagnostic naming the cause and the two remedies (install perl for sub-second resolution, or raise the fixture size until both baselines exceed 0 ms) and exit 3 rather than emitting a number.

HANDOFF.md is written with no terminating newline: the render block's output is captured in a command substitution, which strips every trailing newline, and _print_literal at :631-633 writes with a bare format string that adds none. Same dropped-trailing-newline mechanism as CA-133, in the sibling writer the CA-027 remediation introduced when it moved HANDOFF.md onto write_atomic. edm-state is the file's only writer, it regenerates on every phase, gate and checkpoint, and the file is git-tracked -- so every diff carries a no-newline-at-end-of-file marker and any appending tool concatenates onto the user's last Notes line. Fix: add a newline-terminating renderer beside _print_literal and use it here; do NOT change _print_literal itself, because the pattern-library splice at :3988 depends on its exact no-newline behaviour. Then assert that the last byte of HANDOFF.md is a newline, and run write-handoff once over every tracked initiative to normalize the committed copies.

cmd_update_patterns re-derives the plugin root from $0 with a command -v fallback, though :62 already computes a BASH_SOURCE-derived SCRIPT_DIR global in the same file that is correct under every invocation shape including source. edm-state is deliberately sourceable -- the dispatch is guarded at :4554 and wave7-smoke.sh:4721 and :4787 source it to unit-test the pattern helpers -- and under source $0 is the sourcing shell, so the resolved patterns directory lands outside the plugin entirely. Latent today only because the tests pass an explicit pattern-file argument to the inner body; the next helper that calls cmd_update_patterns on a sourced edm-state gets a silent pattern-file-not-found skip at :4085 and a passing exit 0. Also an instance of the derivation-divergence class CA-049 raised. Fix: delete :4053-4060 and use the existing global.

mermaid_line_set (:172-175) and marker_line_set (:177-180) have zero call sites anywhere in bin/, evals/, bin/tests/ or any prose surface; only their third sibling ignored_line_set is consumed. The library docstring at :38-45 says all three exist so that all three consumers derive the ignored, mermaid and marker sets identically, citing CA-156 -- but the only consumer that needs the mermaid and marker sets, edm-lint-artifacts, DELIBERATELY declines to use them and documents why at :283-292: routing through three per-class functions would cost three extra per-file awk invocations against the documented 3,000 ms commit-path and 60,000 ms CI budgets, so it derives all four projections from one table instead. Neither statement is wrong on its own terms; the result is two dead exports in a shared library, which invites the next contributor onto the slow path. Fix: delete both, or keep them and replace the docstring claim with the real position.

two structurally unreachable guards, one in each standalone checker. edm-check-grants:103 dies on an unexpected extra argument, but every path through the parser at :88-102 leaves the argument count at zero: it was already zero so the block is skipped, or --list-sources required exactly one and then shifted, or an unknown flag died at :96, or a positional died at :99 -- and under this file's set -u the positional reference at :103 would itself raise an unbound-variable error if it were ever reached, confirming the line has never executed. edm-check-vocabulary:191-194's no-files-found message and its exit 0 are dead for the same reason: SCOPE_ROOTS at :105-114 includes two plain files that the build loop appends unconditionally at :184-185 and dies at :187 on any root that is neither a file nor a directory, so the collection always holds at least two entries. Contrast edm-lint-artifacts:105, whose identically worded die sits inside a real loop over multiple arguments and IS reachable, so this is not a project-wide defensive idiom. Fix: delete both; same class, adjacent files, one commit.

a dead defensive default applied to an arithmetic expansion: :244 computes a kilobyte figure with shell arithmetic, which always produces a non-empty string (or, on a malformed operand, a hard shell error -- and the enclosing block runs under set -e from :225), so the empty-value default at :245 can never substitute. Exactly the class the ledger already accepted as a P2 at CA-140. Confidence medium only because the block runs under whatever POSIX shell the runner selects and could not be executed here; on every POSIX shell the expansion yields a value or fails. Fix: delete :245.

git-lock-check removes .git/index.lock on a raced, wrong liveness oracle with no age threshold and no confirmation gate. Three problems on a destructive path: between the process probe and the removal a git add or commit can start and take the lock, so the removal deletes a LIVE lock and permits a second concurrent index write; the oracle is wrong in both directions, because matching only processes named exactly git misses git-remote-https, git-upload-pack, an IDE's embedded libgit2 or JGit and any wrapper-renamed git that can legitimately hold the lock, while also matching git processes belonging to unrelated repositories anywhere on the host and needlessly refusing the remediation; and the classic staleness signal, the lock file's modification time, is never consulted. The comment at :3097-3098 documents the heuristic but not the race, so the false-alarm filter's documented-as-intentional criterion is not met. Fix: require an age threshold before acting, scope liveness to this repository, remove via a rename-aside so a losing racer cannot delete a lock a winner just took, and print the lock's age and holder evidence first. See also CA-247, the wiring half.

an empty array summed in jq yields null, not 0, and every sum in the four metrics renderers is unguarded (:2525-2527, :2537-2538, :2619-2621, :2643-2644) -- while cmd_init writes an empty phase_durations object at :1493. So EVERY freshly initialized initiative renders literal nulls and a dollar-null in place of a duration and a cost, from both metrics-report --all and metrics-report for a single prefix. This fails the consistent-project-pattern test of the false-alarm filter rather than passing it: get_session_tokens_since applies the null-coalescing default correctly at :335-339 and :365-369, so the guard IS the house pattern and these four sites are the omission. The --with-human-baseline savings arms are safe only by accident, because a null comparison is false, which routes them to a not-applicable string by luck rather than by design. Fix: apply the same null-coalescing default to every sum in these four blocks.

the credential probe is the one untimed model call in a driver whose entire contract is per-phase timeouts: every other claude invocation goes through run_with_timeout at :295, this one does not. On a hung connection it blocks indefinitely, the driver never sets its started flag, so the EXIT trap's partial-artifact path at :149-152 is skipped, and eval:nightly burns its whole 150-minute job timeout and fails as a GitLab timeout -- indistinguishable from the slow-phase case CA-063 was filed to make distinguishable, and with no run.json written at all, which then reads as complete via CA-064's still-open absent-file branch. Fix: bound the probe with a short timeout and die naming the missing auth. Note run_with_timeout is defined at :255, AFTER this check, so either move the definition above the credential gate or inline a bounded poll.

archive (:2474) and migrate-path (:2852, with rollback at :2859 and :2866) both rename the initiative directory via git_aware_mv OUTSIDE any with_state_lock acquisition, and the lockbase is derived from state_file_for -- which the move itself changes. A concurrent checkpoint-if-active (the Stop and PreCompact hooks fire unprompted), record-partial-verdict or write-handoff on the same initiative therefore holds a lockdir that the rename relocates WHILE IT IS HELD, so its trap targets a path that no longer exists and the lockdir is leaked at the destination -- inside the archived tree, where nothing will ever reclaim it -- and its staging mktemp fails with a missing-directory error mid-write, which write_atomic reports at :546 as a generic mktemp failure naming none of the actual cause. Neither command serializes against this nor detects it. migrate-path additionally leaves the product directory it created at :2849 in place when it rolls back, and deletes the carried-over backup at :2862 before the write that the rollback at :2866 would want it for. Fix: hold with_state_lock around the check-and-move in both commands, and remove the lockdir before the rename rather than letting it travel with the tree.

the whole-directory token fallback line-caps the CONCATENATION rather than each file, contradicting its own comment at :350 which states that each file is independently line-capped for the same reason as the scoped branch above. With more than one session file the cap keeps only the tail of the final file and silently discards every earlier session's assistant messages -- exactly the sum this fallback exists to produce. Concatenating files without trailing newlines also splices two JSON objects into one unparseable line, which the tolerant parse counts as bad and, per CA-185, downgrades attribution_mode with no indication that tokens were lost. Related boundary in the same area: EDM_TOKEN_READ_LINE_CAP set to 0 satisfies the digits-only validator at :317 and makes the tail emit nothing, so tokens are recorded as 0, which state_anomalies then reports as the BLOCKING zero-tokens anomaly at :1201-1212 -- a configuration value the validator accepts producing a blocking validate failure with no connection back to the cause. Fix: loop the files and cap each one, or correct the comment to say the cap is global; and reject 0 in the validator with a message naming the zero-tokens consequence.

watch-impl's poll collapses three distinguishable outcomes into one: discarding stderr and forcing success means no new ticket commits, a git log failure, and an unresolvable starting revision all read identically. If the branch is rebased or amended and the old commit becomes unreachable and is later pruned, the range query fails on every subsequent poll and the monitor emits NOTHING for the remaining lifetime of the session -- the same indistinguishable-silence failure CA-083 fixed for the initial read (:2484-2486 now hard-fails) but which survives in the loop. Because CLAUDE.md documents the monitor as running for the whole session with no EDM-side kill switch, the silence is permanent and nothing signals that implementation progress is no longer being surfaced. Secondary: the starting revision advances only when a matching commit is found (:2493), so a long run of non-ticket commits makes the scanned range grow without bound, one query over an ever-larger range every five seconds. Fix: capture the exit status, verify the revision still exists, re-anchor to HEAD with one diagnostic line when history was rewritten, and advance on every successful poll rather than only on a match.

with_state_lock's flock branch uses 99 as its lock-timeout sentinel: the subshell exits 99 when flock cannot acquire within the wait, and the caller then reports a lock timeout for any captured status of 99 -- so a locked body that exits 99 for its own reasons is reported as a lock timeout that never happened. 99 is reserved nowhere in the codebase, and the locked bodies already use out-of-band return codes (_cmd_init_body returns 10 at :1524), so the sentinel space is in active use rather than theoretical. Fix: use a distinct out-of-band value and assert in bin/tests/ that no locked body returns it, or better, detect the timeout by testing for the lock's presence rather than by exit code.

twenty refusal assertions in the two suites never swept onto check_fails assert the MESSAGE and discard the exit code: wave5-smoke.sh lines 49-50, 52-53, 55-56, 58-59, 71-72, 120-121, 124-125, 138-139 and 140-141, and wave4a-smoke.sh lines 49-50, 68-69, 91-92, 93-94, 95-96, 97-98, 178-179, 180-181 and 276-277. Each captures combined output with a trailing or-true and substring-matches it, so a regression where migrate-path PRINTS its must-contain-only diagnostic as a warning and then performs the move passes the test. Only two of the eleven wave5 sites carry a companion post-condition that would notice (:63 and :137 assert nothing escaped the SRD root); the other nine, including all three path-traversal input validations and the duplicate-target guard, have no post-condition at all. check_fails (_harness.sh:134-153) does exactly the right thing -- non-zero exit AND case-insensitive message from ONE invocation -- and its own header explains why an exit-code-only assertion is insufficient; it is used roughly thirty times across wave6 and wave7 and these two suites were never migrated. Same class as CA-043, which round 2 closed at a single wave7 site. Fix: mechanical substitution to check_fails, preferring check_refuses_and_leaves_state for the five state-mutating cases so the post-condition is proven from the same execution.

two residual weak assertions inside otherwise-strong new blocks. (1) The CA-039 all-invalid-corpus case asserts the dimension-3 score is merely less than 100 where the value is computable and should be exactly 0 -- the only non-literal expectation in a block whose three siblings all assert hand-computed exact values with the arithmetic spelled out, so a scorer returning 99 for an all-invalid corpus passes. (2) At :2287, inside the T44 AC4 case, the expected-line extraction runs unguarded under set -e while the sibling actual-value capture two lines below is correctly bracketed by an errexit-suspending pair; the loop globs every invalid fixture but the marker-existence loop at :2270-2275 covers only the six hardcoded names, so a seventh invalid fixture added without the expected-line marker CRASHES the suite instead of failing it. Fix: assert exactly 0 with the derivation in a comment, and move the extraction inside the existing bracket with a named failure when it comes back empty.

the CA-141 remediation introduced a NEW path name that no .gitignore pattern matches, no trap covers, no test enumerates and nothing ever cleans: the stale-lock aside directory created by the rename at :984, plus its pattern-library twin under docs/audit-patterns/. Walked every pattern against a realistic path -- the lock-file line, the lockdir line (whose trailing slash makes it an exact-name directory match that the suffixed name defeats), the state-temp line, the markdown-temp line, and the audit-patterns and docs lines -- and none matches. Accumulation risk is real: the rename runs at :984 BEFORE the lock trap is installed at :1025-1028, so no signal handler covers the window between the rename and the unchecked removal, and a group-writable shared checkout where the rename succeeds but the contents belong to another user leaves it permanently and silently. A grep for the stale infix across plugins/edm/ returns only the comment at :950 and the code at :984, with no test at all, and the CA-141a case at wave7-smoke.sh:4311-4345 asserts the lockdir is absent after a reclaim without asserting absence of the aside. One directory accrues per reclaiming PID, inside a TRACKED artifact directory, and it shows in git status forever. Reachable on any host without flock(1). CA-169's single prescribed action never landed: nothing at the flock site records that the lock file must NOT be unlinked. the new retention prune sits after the completion flag is set at :452 and after the exit-4 return at :446, so it runs ONLY on the success path. A developer iterating on prompt changes against a flaky backend, or a scheduled job whose auth expired, accumulates one directory per attempt forever. The false-alarm filter was applied and is not satisfied: the in-code rationale at :545-548 justifies never deleting the run currently under investigation, which is preserved for free by newest-first ordering, and does not justify skipping the prune entirely. the CA-160 injection probe writes and checks a FIXED /tmp proof path at :4659, :4666 and :4668 -- the only scratch path in this 4,891-line suite that ignores TMPDIR, where every sibling uses the honored form or the trap-covered scratch root established at :22-23, so the false-alarm filter's used-consistently-everywhere test fails and this is an inconsistency rather than a project pattern. Three consequences: the path is never pre-cleaned, so any stale copy from an earlier run killed between the write and the check, or from an unrelated process, produces a permanent false FAIL of a blocking assertion on the loudest possible message (that the malformed rate was executed); on a multi-user host user A's leftover file is not removable by user B, whose cleanup silently no-ops; and any local user can plant the file to redden the pipeline. The direction is fail-loud rather than fail-open, which caps this at P2. Fix: derive the proof path inside the suite's own trap-covered scratch tree, remove it immediately before the probe, and interpolate it into the payload so the assertion is self-contained and unique per run.
